articles.title: Behind closed doors, Sweden's Left and Centre parties are still miles apart
articles.summary: The so-called 'red-green' parties of Sweden's left and centre-left wing have been keeping silent about any meetings about forming a government that may or may not be happening. But an unnamed Left Party source says the Centre Party still 'refuses to meet' with them.

articles.title: IN PICS: Seven cups of coffee and sponge cake as government talks begin
articles.summary: Andreas Norlén, the speaker of the Swedish parliament, offered party leaders coffee and a 'sockerkaka' spongecake he had baked himself when he called in seven party leaders to preliminary talks on a new government.

articles.title: Magdalena Andersson first leader tasked with forming new Swedish government
articles.summary: Sweden's parliamentary speaker, Andreas Norlén has tasked Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson with trying to build a new government after a day of talks with the country's party leaders.

articles.title: 'I am available to form a new government': Swedish opposition leader meets speaker
articles.summary: The leading candidate to be Sweden's new Prime Minister, Magdalena Andersson, has declared herself 'available' to form a new government after she held the first party leader meeting with the parliament's speaker after the election.

articles.title: OPINION: Yes, Swedish immigrants vote in their own interests – just like other voters
articles.summary: Data shows that voters in Sweden with foreign backgrounds support left-wing parties in often much higher numbers than they do right-wing parties. The Local's Mandy Pipher says, 'So what?'

articles.title: Swedish parliamentary speaker to meet party leaders – Andersson first
articles.summary: Following Ulf Kristersson’s request to be relieved of his duties as Prime Minister, the process of appointing a new Prime Minister is now underway, with the house speaker inviting party leaders to individual meetings today.

articles.title: IN DATA: Did foreign voters lose the election for Sweden's right-wing government?
articles.summary: Senior politicians for the far-right Sweden Democrats have reacted to the party's poor election result by blaming immigrant voters and newly naturalised Swedish citizens voting for the first time. Is there any truth to this?

articles.title: Kristersson resigns as PM after Sweden's centre-left opposition wins election
articles.summary: Sweden's prime minister Ulf Kristersson has tendered his resignation as the vote count for Sweden's election was completed shortly after 1pm on Thursday, with the opposition parties retaining their 176-173 lead over the government bloc.

articles.title: Jimmie Åkesson reportedly plans break if Sweden Democrats enter opposition
articles.summary: Several sources within the Sweden Democrats have told the TV4 broadcaster that their leader Jimmie Åkesson is expected to take a break if the party ends up in opposition.

articles.title: Sweden's Tidö bloc faces '99.9% certain' defeat as final vote counting continues
articles.summary: With the count almost finished, public broadcaster SVT's election forecast states that the probability of the centre-left opposition securing the most seats is 99.9 percent.

articles.title: OPINION: Sweden's misunderstood Centre Party could learn from Ebba Busch
articles.summary: The Centre Party is the kingmaker for Sweden's next government, but it has boxed itself in with red lines in all directions. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist should learn from Ebba Busch if she wants to find a way out, argues The Local's James Savage.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Could the extra 'Wednesday votes' really flip Sweden's election?
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of extra votes are being counted in the Swedish election on Wednesday and Thursday. Could this change the outcome?

articles.title: Swedish politics professor: 'I don't see a plausible alternative to the left-leaning quartet'
articles.summary: Sweden's right-wing parties are suggesting Magdalena Andersson will fail to form a coalition, allowing them to win over the Centre Party. In this Q&A, professor Nicholas Aylott explains why he thinks that's wishful thinking.

articles.title: Just how big were the Sweden Democrats' losses in the Swedish election?
articles.summary: The Sweden Democrats are the biggest losers in the general election, with the party losing ground in 285 of Sweden's 290 municipalities.

articles.title: Social Democrats demand that Swedish PM concedes defeat and resigns
articles.summary: Sweden's leading opposition party, the Social Democrats, has demanded that Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson concede defeat in the country's national election as the last votes to be counted look less and less likely to overturn the opposition's three-seat lead.

articles.title: Sweden starts counting final batch of votes in tight election
articles.summary: Election officials in Sweden started counting the the last early and overseas votes on Wednesday, but the count isn't expected to be finished until Thursday.

articles.title: 'It's tighter than I thought': How do foreigners in Sweden feel about the election?
articles.summary: The votes are still being counted after a tense election campaign. We asked The Local's readers how they feel about the results so far.

articles.title: What does Sweden's unexpectedly close election result mean for foreigners?
articles.summary: As it stands right now, a 'Tidö 2' government lacks a mandate, as does the Centre Party's dream 'middle government', and two of the four opposition parties who could form a majority refuse to rule together. If nothing changes, what does this mean for foreigners in Sweden?

articles.title: Swedish government scenarios: What happens now?
articles.summary: The centre-left is in the lead 176-173 seats, but it's unclear who will be able to form a government. The Local explains what the future might hold.

articles.title: Swedish word of the day: talmansrunda
articles.summary: The word 'talmansrunda' is crucial vocabulary if you want to have any hope of understanding how a prime minister gets appointed in Sweden.

articles.title: EU Commission mulls revision of Schengen visa rules and fees
articles.summary: The European Commission is planning a revision of Schengen rules on short-stay visas to make the EU’s visa policy "more coherent, secure and effective, while facilitating legitimate travel".

articles.title: What does Sweden's unexpectedly close election result mean for foreigners?
articles.summary: As it stands right now, a 'Tidö 2' government lacks a mandate, as does the Centre Party's dream 'middle government', and two of the four opposition parties who could form a majority refuse to rule together. If nothing changes, what does this mean for foreigners in Sweden?

articles.title: OPINION: Sweden's election won't erase what the last four years did to immigrants
articles.summary: On Sunday, Sweden will make a choice with profound implications for foreigners living here — and the latest polls show it could go either way. But don’t imagine the problems will evaporate with a change of government, says James Savage.

articles.title: Politics in Sweden: Immigration is on the agenda, but the debate is surreal
articles.summary: SVT's televised immigration debate showed being tough on immigration isn't a straightforward vote-winner any longer. But by focusing almost entirely on refugees, the debate managed to ignore the people who actually migrate to Sweden in the 2020s, writes The Local's James Savage.

articles.title: 'We don't want people who are integrated in Sweden to be forced to leave'
articles.summary: The Social Democrats want to launch a fast-track investigation into residency for people who have lived in the country for a long time in a bid to solve teen deportation and Brexit cases, the party's migration spokesperson has told The Local.

articles.title: Five EU countries aim to send rejected migrants to 'return hubs' by 2027
articles.summary: Five European Union countries are seeking a deal with an unnamed non-EU country to host a "return hub" for migrants whose asylum applications have been rejected, with a targeted start date of January 1, a Danish minister said Friday.

articles.title: Social Democrats plan huge inquiry to clean up Swedish immigration law
articles.summary: The Social Democrats are planning to launch a government inquiry which will carry out a major review of the country's migration legislation, arguing that years of piecemeal reforms have made the rules unnecessarily complicated and contradictory.

articles.title: Social Democrats promise new 'expat welcome desk' in Stockholm
articles.summary: The Social Democrats have said if they win the election in Stockholm as well as regional elections, they will set up a new 'expat welcome desk' for foreign workers arriving in the city.

articles.title: How to appeal if your application for Swedish citizenship is rejected
articles.summary: Many, perhaps most, of the 100,000 people in the queue when the new citizenship law came into force on June 6th will not meet the new requirements, meaning there's likely to be a wave of rejections. Here's what to do if your application is rejected.

articles.title: 'Sweden has fulfilled its commitments': Migration minister defends Brexit deportations
articles.summary: Sweden's migration minister has defended the country's unusually high refusal rate for post-Brexit residency in response to a parliamentary question asking what action he will take to stop high profile deportations of elderly British citizens.

articles.title: OPINION: Sweden keeps bodging its migration laws – it needs to do better
articles.summary: Time and again, Swedish migration laws lead to people whom nearly everyone agrees should be allowed to stay being forced out the country. Sweden needs to do better, says James Savage.

articles.title: 'Ripped from a loved one': British-Swedish couple separated by Brexit deportation
articles.summary: Three and a half months after John and Caroline Sellers got married, John was deported from Sweden, a country he had lived in since he was ten years old. They are one of many couples separated by Sweden's strict application of Brexit rules.

articles.title: Sweden's Green Party calls for return of safety clause to limit Brexit deportations
articles.summary: Green Party immigration spokesperson Annika Hirvonen has called for Sweden to reinstate the humanitarian safety clause abolished in 2023, arguing that this would prevent the deportation of elderly British citizens like Horace 'George' Mason and Joyce Thomas.

articles.title: 'Dividing families': Iranian academics slam Sweden's 'medieval' family immigration laws
articles.summary: Shima and Bijan left the UK for Sweden seven years ago with their young daughter. If they knew then what they know now about Sweden's approach to family immigration, they say they would never have come.

articles.title: What's causing Sweden's second wave of post-Brexit deportations?
articles.summary: The plight of the estimated 4,000 British citizens refused post-Brexit residency rights is seeing a renewed surge in media attention, with cases reported in the UK and Swedish media. What's behind this second wave of Brexit deportations?

articles.title: Sweden awards fewer than 100 new citizenships the month after new rules come into force
articles.summary: Fewer than 100 Swedish citizenship applications – and only 20 through naturalisation – were approved in July, the month after new and stricter citizenship rules came into force.

articles.title: Integration investigator says Swedish for Immigrants needs redesign
articles.summary: Language studies in SFI must be combined with concrete social orientation in order to get more foreign-born people, especially in vulnerable areas, integrated into society, according to Bi Puranen, research leader at the World Values ​​Survey.

articles.title: Swedish government wins vote on 'cruel' family immigration bill
articles.summary: The government and the Sweden Democrats won the vote on stricter requirements for family immigration on August 13th, despite a strong united opposition to two of its key proposals which opposition parties called 'cruel.'

articles.title: 'If you came to work in Sweden because of relaxed citizenship rules, I don’t want you'
articles.summary: In the first of The Local's election interviews with the immigration spokespeople of Sweden's political parties, the Sweden Democrats' Ludvig Aspling downplays the impacts of new stricter work permit and citizenship rules on skilled labour migrants, and outlines his party's plans for the next mandate period.

articles.title: 'I feel shame and rage': Immigration clampdown hits Swedes close to home
articles.summary: Gustav and Luisa have worked hard to build a life together in Sweden with their young son, but after a surprise rejection of Luisa's permanent residency application, they tell The Local they now fear for their family's future.

articles.title: Centre-left holds on to power in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö
articles.summary: The balance of power looks set to hold in the country's three largest municipalities, all of which are governed by centre-left coalitions.

articles.title: What you need to know about the local and regional elections in Gothenburg
articles.summary: The regional elections in Gothenburg and the surrounding region see the red-green coalitions which took power in 2022 defending their record on healthcare, traffic management, schools, and elderly care, as the right-wing parties try to limit further gains.

articles.title: Self-driving bus crashes with tram in Gothenburg on first day
articles.summary: A self-driving bus was involved in a crash with a tram on its first day carrying passengers in the Swedish city of Gothenburg.

articles.title: 'An international hub': These are the best districts for foreigners in Gothenburg
articles.summary: Majorna, the long-gentrified former working class district of central Gothenburg, and the adjoining Linné have been ranked the best district for foreigners in the city by readers of The Local, although many readers also rated Hisingen as a convenient and comfortable place to settle.

articles.title: What's that haze in the air in Gothenburg?
articles.summary: Swedish newspapers are reporting that for three days there's been a thick layer of smog covering the west coast city of Gothenburg.

articles.title: Gothenburg council withdraws monkey images after racism accusations
articles.summary: Social services in north-eastern Gothenburg were criticised for structural racism after using monkeys instead of humans in counselling material for children and young people in the area.

articles.title: Five reasons Sweden should move its capital to Gothenburg
articles.summary: Historically Stockholm was a natural choice for Sweden's capital. But times have changed. Here are the some of the reasons why Sweden should switch its political and business centre to Gothenburg, the gateway to Scandinavia.

articles.title: Which Swedish cities are most popular among young professionals?
articles.summary: A new study from Stockholm-based research company Future Place Leadership listed Gothenburg as the most attractive Swedish city to live and work in.

articles.title: 'Stay home' warning as Storm Louis blows roof off Gothenburg station
articles.summary: Police have warned people to stay inside as Storm Louis batters western Sweden, blowing parts of the roof off Gothenburg Central Station.

articles.title: Dead body found after fire at Gothenburg's Liseberg amusement park
articles.summary: One person has been found dead after a fire destroyed Liseberg's new water park Oceana, which had been set to open this summer.

articles.title: One man missing after fire inferno at Sweden's biggest amusement park
articles.summary: A man is missing after a fire broke out at the Liseberg amusement park in Gothenburg, with shocking images showing its newly built water park in flames.

articles.title: 'Unique' Viking graves change what we know about central Gothenburg
articles.summary: Swedish archaeologists have described two Viking graves as 'unique' after they were discovered in central Gothenburg, shedding new light on the history of Sweden’s second-largest city.

articles.title: Heartwarming story about Gothenburg's public library goes viral
articles.summary: What do you do if the library is officially closed but you manage to sneak in anyway? Borrow books, of course.

articles.title: TRAVEL: Number of daily trains between Oslo and Gothenburg to double
articles.summary: The number of daily train departures between the Norwegian capital of Oslo and the Swedish city of Gothenburg will double this winter, rail company Vy announced Thursday.

articles.title: How to have a cheap holiday in Sweden this summer
articles.summary: Things are looking better in the Swedish economy, but many households are still feeling the pinch. No matter the size of your budget, you don't have to miss out on all the fun this summer.

articles.title: Christmas in Sweden 2025: The best julbord in the Gothenburg area
articles.summary: Whether you're a Swedish Christmas newbie or a seasoned julbord connoisseur, here's The Local's selection of some of the best (often fishy) festive meals in the Gothenburg area this winter. Feel free to share other tips in the comments!

articles.title: Why is 'everyone called Glenn' in Gothenburg?
articles.summary: We find out if everyone in Gothenburg is really called Glenn and where the old joke comes from.

articles.title: Moving to Gothenburg? The best areas and neighbourhoods to live in
articles.summary: Whether you're moving to Sweden’s second biggest city for the first time or are looking for another neighbourhood, The Local talks you through some of your best options.

articles.title: Five great day trips to do from Gothenburg
articles.summary: Gothenburg has a lively culture scene, plenty of green spaces and food and drink in abundance, but sometimes you just need to escape the city. The West Coast and nearby towns provide plenty of opportunities for a memorable day trip from Sweden's second city: here are five of our favourite destinations complete with insider tips.

articles.title: The story of the biggest fire disaster in Swedish history
articles.summary: At a Halloween party in Gothenburg in 1998, a fire started by four youths led to one of the deadliest disasters of modern Swedish history. Sixty-three young people lost their lives and many more were injured.
